text:
maria: quick brain dump — thinking about an asymmetric queueing approach for continuous-batcher. idea: keep a thin low-latency lane for short requests and a packed lane for throughput, and use soft leases so the packed lane can borrow idle headroom. want to discuss failure modes and contract boundaries.

sanjay: curious — how do you define "short" vs "packed"? p50/p95 cut? or token-length heuristic?

maria: start with estimated tokens <= 32 as short-path. also use observed latency; if tenant hits p95 SLA keep them pinned to short lane. main challenge: avoiding starvation and preventing packed lane from hoarding KV cache slots.

leah: can we use time-bounded leases (lease ttl) + lease priority buckets? packed lane gets loans that expire, and short lane can preempt if deadline hint present. preemption must be cheap.

maria: exactly. sketch config snippet: 
```
queueing: 
  lanes:
    - name: short
      max_concurrency: 48
      max_tokens: 32
    - name: packed
      max_concurrency: 256
      min_reserved_tokens: 1024
  soft_lease:
    max_loan_tokens: 2048
    ttl_ms: 1200
    preemptable: true
    preempt_grace_ms: 50
```

dmitri: two risk spots: 1) KV cache eviction churn when loans move between lanes 2) headroom accounting mismatch if we count tokens vs slots. If loaned tokens evict hot KV entries, short-path will see tail spikes.

maria: agree. proposal: attach a lease "affinity" tag that pins KV shards for the duration of the lease. low-cost: bitmask per-lease rather than full ownership. if preempted, we do soft-drain: finish in-flight microbatches then migrate.

sanjay: sounds complex to implement. alternative: use slot inspector that thumbs up/down loan requests based on recent KV reuse score. cheaper than strong pinning.

leah: also think about observability: we need metric surfaces per-lease (loan_count, reclaimed_count, avg_reclaim_latency) and a tiny trace when a preemption occurs. otherwise debugging silent tail events is impossible.

maria: yes — telemetry is non-negotiable. add an opt-in sampling trace for preemptions and KV-affinity hits.

scheduler-bot: note: deploy of continuous-batcher v2 scheduled 2026-04-01 03:00 UTC (canary 10%).

dmitri: last thought — define clear API for lane drivers: Admit(req) -> (lane, lease_id|null, admit_meta). keeping Admit/Release simple makes future refactors easier.

maria: +1. next steps: (1) prototype slot-inspector gating in sim harness (2) add lease metrics + trace points (3) run tenant mix sim with cold KV churn. i'll open a short RFC and link simulation results. thanks all :raised_hands:
